name: Central Buttress
text: [overview] Descent, fastest: 20 minutes north on the Continental Divide, then Andrews Glacier and Andrews Creek.
[overview] Alternatively walk ten minutes to the North Gully, downclimb its first 100' (steep snow), then descend 800' by plunge-stepping to the base snowfield.

name: Cold Blooded Boys
text: [overview] Approach: follow the trail up Glacier Gorge to Green Lake, climb the North Gully that separates Pagoda Mountain from the Keyboard of the Winds to sit below Sievers' Tower, then cross east beneath the Keyboards.

name: South Face
text: [overview] Depending on the year, possibly the gentlest, most secure line up the peak: tidy scrambling plus moderate snow in place of the northwest gully's ice and rubble.

name: Alpine Ambition
text: [detailed_rack] A picket may help, since many cruxes begin on steep snow that is firm, with scant protection before several insecure moves.

name: Grendel's Lair
text: [approach] The usual way in follows that drainage, which is steep, brushy and slow, and in a dry early winter it can be mostly free of snow.
[approach] The ice starts as a low notch at the foot of the Northwest Couloir and grows down toward the snowfield below.
[descent_text] Once down at the steep snow ramp above the first pitch, stroll down and around the gentle snowfield back to the foot of the climb.

[descent_text] A walk-off is also possible from the top: leave the notch and go left over the diamond-shaped wall, which is snowy third-class ground that is best done with plenty of daylight or route-finding experience.

name: Ptarmigan Song
text: [overview] Follow steep snow up the gully about one rope length to an exit gully that breaks right from the main one.
[overview] Mixed climbing through that exit gully gives access to the adjacent gully, which runs to the summit across moderate snow and ice runnels totaling 1500'.
[approach] Overhangs cap both walls of the dihedral, but a line of ice slips between them to a choke below a moderate snow slope.
[approach] Do not follow the obvious snow line that ends at a gap in the ridge to the summit's west;

name: Curving Vine
text: [approach] Scramble around the north side of the lake beneath the east face and aim for North Chimney, the hidden gully below the middle of the Diamond with a snow tongue reaching into it;
[approach] North Chimney is loose fourth and low fifth class (about 5.4) with snow early in the season, so keep out from under other parties and expect rockfall.
[descent_text] Four more rappels end on the snowfield;

name: D7
text: [approach] Scramble around the north side of the lake beneath the east face and aim for North Chimney, the hidden gully below the middle of the Diamond with a snow tongue reaching into it;

text: [approach] Scramble around the north side of the lake beneath the east face and aim for North Chimney, the hidden gully below the middle of the Diamond with a snow tongue reaching into it;
[approach] North Chimney is loose fourth and low fifth class (about 5.4) with snow early in the season, so keep out from under other parties and expect rockfall.

name: Dicker's Peck
text: [overview] A pinnacle in the notch to the north of Navajo, visible while hiking the trail up Isabel Glacier.
[overview] Reach the notch by a snow route, the most direct being Navajo Snowfield at 45 degrees, or by the East Ledges line on Apache, once it has melted out.
[overview] Descend by scrambling to Navajo's summit and down the loose Airplane gully, which holds an old plane wreck and returns to where the snow climbs begin.

name: East Face/Dallas Peak
text: [overview] A snowy couloir reaches the crest;

name: East Prow
text: [approach] Start at the Glacier Gorge trailhead on Bear Lake Road and follow the Glacier Gorge trail about 5 miles to Black Lake.

name: Endless Summer
text: [overview] Seven pitches from Mill's Glacier.
[overview] scramble about 100 feet northward downhill to a 2-bolt anchor, and rap three more times to Mill's Glacier.

name: Field's Chimney
text: [approach] Continue past the lake to Mills Glacier.
[descent_text] From there, the rappel line down the lower east face reaches Mills Glacier with two ropes;

name: Fields' Chimney (summer)
text: [overview] Funnel-shaped chimney at the right-hand limit of that wall, reached over Mills Glacier and followed for multiple pitches up to Broadway.

name: Ptarmigan Glacier
text: [overview] What is left of an ancient glacier, tucked at the far western curve of the cirque.
[detailed_rack] carry pickets to protect it.
[approach] Stay on the path and cairns, or the easiest line when snow covers them, to the foot of a snowfield at the south end of the base of Notchtop Spire.
[approach] That is the lower glacier.
[approach] From its top, bear up and a little right to reach the foot of the steeper upper glacier.
[approach] These are steep snow slopes in avalanche terrain, so check the avalanche forecast first.

name: Dragon's Tooth (aka Dead Elk Couloir)
text: [detailed_rack] One picket, mountaineering axes, and small to medium tricams for a short three-move rock section.
[approach] Follow the right side of the lake, taking care with water running under the snow and ice.
[approach] A snow cornice can form at the top.

name: Forgotten Arete
text: [overview] Approach: follow the trail through Glacier Gorge toward Green Lake, ascend the North Gully, which lies between Pagoda Mountain and the Keyboard of the Winds, to the foot of Sievers' Tower, then go east along the foot of the Keyboards to Jackpot Tower.

name: Forgotten North Face
text: [overview] Approach: Glacier Gorge toward Green Lake, up the North Gully between Pagoda Mountain and the Keyboard of the Winds to the foot of Sievers' Tower, then east along the foot of the Keyboards to Mrs.

name: Forrest Finish
text: [approach] Scramble around the north side of the lake beneath the east face and aim for North Chimney, the hidden gully below the middle of the Diamond with a snow tongue reaching into it;
[approach] North Chimney is loose fourth and low fifth class (about 5.4) with snow early in the season, so keep out from under other parties and expect rockfall.
[descent_text] From Table Ledge, follow the D7 rappel line (five double-rope rappels) to Broadway, then four rappels beside North Chimney down to the glacier.

name: Fourth Flatiron East Face AKA The Watercourse
Black Lake Slabs
peak: Glacier Creek Drainage including Black Lake area
text: [approach] From the Glacier Gorge parking area, follow the trail to Black Lake, then carry on around to the lake's east side and climb the drainage that leads toward Spearhead.
[descent_text] The simplest way down is to reverse the climb through the snow, with a few short, low-exposure ice downclimbs.
[descent_text] Climbing past the end of the ice and descending the gully beside Spearhead is also possible, but it adds a long stretch of deep snow.

name: Black Lake - West Gully
peak: Glacier Creek Drainage including Black Lake area
text: [approach] Take the trail from the Glacier Gorge parking area to Black Lake.
[approach] The approach is long, and skis help on the way out when there is enough snow.
[approach] Slopes below the climb can be loaded with snow.

name: Duncan's Dinky Drip
peak: Glacier Creek Drainage including Black Lake area
text: [overview] Found within Glacier Gorge on its south side, with Reflections a few minutes west of it.
[overview] scramble over a snowy ledge, then choose a line up the upper curtain, around 30' high.
[approach] The ice is on the south side of Glacier Gorge, only a few minutes east of Reflections.
[approach] It forms as two short curtains with a snowy ledge between them.

name: Stoneman
peak: Glacier Creek Drainage including Black Lake area
text: [approach] Take the Glacier Gorge trail to the lake and look up at the back wall.

name: The Nickcicle
peak: Glacier Creek Drainage including Black Lake area
text: [approach] It can be seen from Black Lake, which you reach by the trail from the Glacier Gorge parking area.

name: Yellow Tears
peak: Glacier Creek Drainage including Black Lake area
text: [approach] The Glacier Gorge trail leads to the lake below.

name: Glacier Gorge Traverse
text: [overview] A ridge traverse around the cirque of Glacier Gorge, from Arrowhead to Longs, with exposed scrambling and climbing.

name: Cornice Bowl, The
text: [overview] A big cornice on the leeward side guards the top, and a slide from it once reached the road.
[overview] The bowl is also a popular spot for crevasse rescue practice.
[approach] A large cornice guards the top, and it has released an avalanche that ran to the road in the past;
[approach] These are steep snow slopes in avalanche terrain, so check the avalanche forecast first.

name: Little Italy
text: [overview] Glen Cove ski classic, a moderate snow climb on a north aspect, named for a shape resembling Italy.
[detailed_rack] A snow picket, plus a light rack if wanted.
[approach] These are steep snow slopes in avalanche terrain, so check the avalanche forecast first.

name: GunRunner Couloir
text: [overview] Real climbing starts roughly halfway up, as the gully draws you in and the snow steepens.

[overview] About two thirds up is a very steep crux, handled either head-on on snow, perhaps with pickets, or by a rock variation on the right, which still carries serious consequences for a fall and few protectable spots.
[detailed_rack] a picket may help on short sections.

name: Cracklin' Otis Bran
text: [overview] Three steps or cruxes early on lead to moderate snow climbing that tops out on Otis Peak.
[overview] Several descents work: Andrew's Glacier, a traverse over to Flattop, or Otis's East Ridge then choose a line down to Lake Haiyaha.

name: Sheep Skin Protection (WW)
text: [overview] Approach by hiking above Lincoln Falls toward the rock glacier's toe, then traversing high across to the foot of the wall.

name: Splitter Choss (WW)
text: [overview] Approach by hiking above Lincoln Falls toward the rock glacier's toe, then traversing high across to the foot of the wall.

name: Thin Pin (WW)
text: [overview] Approach by hiking above Lincoln Falls toward the rock glacier's toe, then traversing high across to the foot of the wall.

name: First Star Couloir
text: [detailed_rack] Optional protection: flukes and pickets.
[approach] Mary's Glacier trailhead walk the steep road to St.
[approach] Mary's Lake, go around its north side, and climb the glacier to the plain of Jamaica Flats.
[approach] These are steep snow slopes in avalanche terrain, so check the avalanche forecast first.

name: Snow Lion
text: [overview] The first is a constriction where the snow separates from the rock and crevasse-like features show;
[overview] The second comes at the ridge crest itself, where the route becomes much steeper and the snow can turn rotten.
[detailed_rack] Three pickets and an 8mm rope of 100'.
[approach] These are steep snow slopes in avalanche terrain, so check the avalanche forecast first.
[descent_text] The northeast slopes route is an easy way down from the summit, and sliding down the neighbouring Gaiteraid couloir returns to the base of Snow Lion.
[descent_text] The top of Snow Lion can be steep and rotten after the sun reaches it, and cornices may form on the ridge.
[descent_text] Carry an axe and crampons.

name: Kiener's Route
text: [overview] From the trailhead, walk to Chasm Lake and around it to Mill's Glacier and the foot of the Lamb's Slide, a 1000 ft snow and ice couloir at about 50 degrees;
[detailed_rack] add a picket or two in winter.
[approach] Skirt Chasm Lake on its north side (in winter the frozen lake can be crossed) to reach Mills Glacier beneath the east face, where Lamb's Slide begins.
[approach] Climb Lamb's Slide, a snow or ice couloir of about 1,000 ft at roughly 50 degrees, to within a couple of hundred feet of its top, then exit right onto Broadway.

name: Krishna Cutoff
text: [overview] Beginner+ alpine outing with some rock, snow, ice and exposure.
[overview] the ramp passes over further crumbly cliffs but is wide and presents no difficulties when snow is firm.

[overview] At first that gully is maybe 50 feet across, then halfway up it shrinks into a tight notch cut into the face, 100-200 feet long: the crux, with snow that runs from firm to unconsolidated, ice patches, and awkward rock moves at Class 3 or 4.
[overview] Continue up steep mixed terrain to the summit, or bail left onto snow slopes and the ridge.
[detailed_rack] Carry an axe, crampons, and a light alpine set of gear plus long slings (several).
[detailed_rack] Short ice screws (two or so) and a picket might help.
